alignments.note: Imperative with its English subject pronoun under rule 17; the *ye* stands immediately after the verb, so it is the verb's and not a vocative's (rule 36).
Short divine name rendered *Jehovah*; the ASV margin's *Hallelujah* gloss is read and set aside under rule 38.
Second imperative with its subject pronoun, as the first.
Object marker with no English of its own; the ASV writes the object bare (rule 16).
Construct noun with a supplied *the*, since no article morpheme stands in the phrase (rule 29).
Third imperative; the *ye* here stands before the vocative noun and is that noun's under rule 36, so the verb keeps only its own word.
Supplied object pronoun with no object morpheme in the clause — the third colon writes no marker and no suffix — so `added` under rule 44.
Vocative noun with its supplied *O* and *ye* (rule 36); the pronoun stands before the noun, which is what allocates it here rather than to the imperative.

review_notes: Three imperatives, two with a following *ye* (the verb's) and one with a preceding *ye* (the vocative's); allocated by adjacency under rule 36.
The supplied *him* of the third colon is `added`: no object marker stands there, unlike the second colon.
